P.h: Langflow flaws let unauthenticated attackers run code, exploit module is public
P.p: IBM reported four Langflow vulnerabilities affecting versions 1.0.0 through 1.12.8. Two are critical and need no account: one bypasses authentication, the other permits arbitrary code execution through MCP tool enumeration. A public Metasploit module already enumerates Langflow MCP tools without credentials.
P.s: Version 1.13.0 is the only fix and it disables automatic login by default. IBM has not published a workaround, so patch now or pull exposed instances off the internet.

items.h: Over 1,000 GitLab servers exposed to active attacks
items.d: A maximum-severity remote code execution flaw in GitLab's CI/CD regular expression compiler is being exploited. Unauthenticated attackers can run code. CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. TLDR InfoSec says custom Ruby deployments need Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12, 4.0.9 or later.

items.h: WorkOS discloses AI-assisted data security incident
items.d: Unauthorized access to an internal sales application on October 30 exposed business contacts, customer account histories and excerpts of customer communications. WorkOS saw an AI-assisted offensive framework automating recon and exploitation. External access is disabled.

items.h: ChatGPT accounts taken over through HTML Preview
items.d: Parameter Labs chained the MathLive library, a YouTube-hosted iframe and oEmbed to bypass the CSP and steal private data. TLDR DevOps says a link was enough to run code as chatgpt.com. OpenAI fixed it on October 26 and rated it P1.

items.h: Revolve says hackers stole payment card details
items.d: Per its SEC filing, attackers used automated methods to take names, contact details and card numbers with expiry dates. Texas lists 127,200 affected residents.

P.h: Cyber-attack defrosts supermarket freezers in seven European countries
P.p: A suspected cyber-attack switched refrigeration evaporators to defrost mode at supermarkets in Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland. Freezer temperatures reportedly reached 50 degrees Celsius, forcing stores to discard food. One Delhaize branch reported 100,000 euros in losses.
P.s: Sabcobel says affected units need physical changes. Remote internet-connected maintenance remains part of the operating model, so the exposure persists.

tiles.d: Atredis found four privilege escalation flaws and two remote code execution bugs in Steam for Windows. A leak plus a stack overflow built a ROP chain. Patched; proof of concept is public.

tiles.t: Cloudflare Q3: more swarms, fewer giants
tiles.d: 18.2 million network DDoS attacks. Short attacks rose 208% year over year; attacks above 1 Tbps fell 69% from Q2.

tiles.t: How Bash could have been backdoored
tiles.d: Hacktron found command injection in GNU Savannah's GPG key validator, gaining root and access to a Bash maintainer's account.

tiles.t: Google pays up to $250,000 for root-in-cloud
tiles.d: Cloud VRP now rewards exploits giving full IAM control over arbitrary tenants or code execution in Borg.
BSI says Bundestag members got Apple threat notifications and should assume compromise.

P.h: OpenAI folds ChatGPT Work into regular Chat and merges Codex limits
P.p: OpenAI is rolling Work capabilities directly into regular Chat while combining usage allowances across ChatGPT and Codex. TLDR IT says the aim is to simplify access to advanced workflows and give subscribers more flexibility.
P.s: Related IT news: ServiceNow and OpenAI expand their partnership to bring governed ServiceNow workflows into ChatGPT, and Gartner warns token-based pricing could push AI costs more than 50% above expectations by 2027.

tiles.t: Google Cloud spend caps now GA
tiles.d: Use the Cloud Billing Budgets API to give each new sandbox project a spending limit.
11 founding partners, including OpenAI, Anthropic and Okta, plan pretested integrations to govern multi-vendor AI.

tiles.t: CrowdStrike and Dell secure the AI Factory
tiles.d: Falcon sold alongside Dell AI infrastructure with NVIDIA, covering workloads, agents and apps.

tiles.t: Gemini Enterprise meets Snowflake via MCP
tiles.d: Agents turn requests into SQL through Cortex while user-level permissions still apply.

tiles.t: Postgres 19 delayed by AI bug reports
tiles.d: A surge of AI-found bugs and patches slips the release; target is November 19.

P.h: Datadog: default to serverless for AI agents, then let production data decide
P.p: Datadog argues serverless should be the first execution model teams evaluate for AI agents. It cites a study of over 35,000 coding agent sessions where LLM or tool calls filled only 20 percent of the median session, so idle time dominates.
P.s: Also this week: Grafana 13.3 adds cross-dashboard variables and Notebooks in public preview, plus a generally available Undo turn for Assistant edits, and Datadog now traces voice agents.

tiles.d: Route public requests to private origin IPs with WAF, caching and bot management, no inbound firewall exceptions.

tiles.t: GKE scales to dense agent workloads
tiles.d: Dataplane V2 avoids Cilium's 65,536 identity limit. Google reports 300 sandboxes per second.
General availability for the kernel-level observability tool.
Fixed in upstream stable kernels October 15. TLDR InfoSec says Ubuntu and RHEL lacked fixed kernels as of November 1.
Static allowlists need three new ranges; Meta API sync picks them up automatically.

items.h: Anthropic warns it is close to recursive self-improvement
items.d: TLDR says an updated S-1 states Anthropic may soon meet its own internal definition of recursive self-improvement, meaning self-building AI.

items.h: OpenAI's Pando cuts Git push latency nearly 5x
items.d: A new backend for Git repositories handles concurrent pushes to many branches and now serves nearly a petabyte of Git data per day.

items.h: Agents collapse tool catalogs into one exec tool
items.d: Models write short scripts that chain and await actions inside isolated sandboxes, instead of single tool calls.

items.d: All-stock AI deal pairing custom AI chips with optical data movement.
